messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — Cross-region routing anomaly detected. 5xx spike + latency for requests originating in EU that should route to eu-west2. Possible routing policy drift. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/cross-region-routing>. Notifying on-call.

jordan: ack, I'm oncall. Investigating now. Where are the spikes (customer/route)?

emma-prod: seeing lots of 504s and timeouts from edge->eu-west2, then many requests get routed to us-central1 which is increasing latency. Examples from logs: /api/generate requests returning 504/502.

raj-net: traceroute from edge -> eu-west2 shows path flip: next-hop changed to transit-us instead of local-eu; BGP flaps? grabbing bgp and route table snapshots.

maria-infra: I deployed geo-steer v2 ~12m ago (canary -> prod). It modified route preference ordering to prefer capacity tiers. Could be policy inversion.

jordan: if geo-steer rollout is suspect, let's roll it back. Who can initiate rollback?

maria-infra: I can trigger rollout rollback. Plan: rollback to geo-steer v1, reduce pin TTL while we validate. Command:```
# rollback geo-steer to v1
redwoodctl rollout rollback --policy geo-steer --to-version v1 --reason "hotfix: routing misroute"
```

ops-bot: Rollback job queued: job_id=rb_987654, initiated_by=maria-infra, started_at=3199990050. Will post status updates.

lucas-cs: Heads-up: customers CUST-A, CUST-B, and CUST-D reported errors within last 10m. CUST-B has an ongoing support ticket (TKT-4523).

jordan: running health probes and synthetic traffic to eu-west2 endpoints. Watching 5xx rate, p95 latency, and host affinity metrics.

emma-prod: after rollback started, some requests are returning 200 again but p95 still ~800ms for a subset pinned to the wrong region.

raj-net: digging into DNS & pinning: I see session pin TTL set to 900s in recent rollout. That means clients pinned to the misrouted region for a long time. We should reduce TTL and force rebind.

maria-infra: reducing pin TTL to 30s now and reloading policy. Command:```
redwoodctl config set policy.geo-steer.session_ttl 30
redwoodctl config reload policy.geo-steer
```

ops-bot: Config reload success. change_id=cfg_334455.

jordan: canary sweep results: synthetic checks success rate back to baseline for 9/10 canaries, p95 improved to ~180ms. Real traffic error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.2% across affected routes.

emma-prod: pushing a small script to invalidate in-memory cache for pinned sessions to accelerate recovery:```
for id in $(cat affected_sessions.txt); do curl -X POST https://edge-internal/clear_pin/$id; done
```

lucas-cs: Notifying flagged customers that we've mitigated and asking for confirmation. Sending proactive status update to all impacted accounts.

jordan: summary of impact so far: ~12 customers showed errors, peak error rate ~12% for eu-bound traffic between 3199990000-3199990120. Root cause likely geo-steer v2 rollout introduced inverted fallback priority plus session_ttl defaulted to 900s which preserved bad pins. Mitigations: rollback to v1, reduce session_ttl to 30s, invalidate pinned sessions, monitor.

maria-infra: follow-ups: 1) add a preflight check to detect inverted route priority, 2) make session_ttl change gated by canary, 3) add an automated rollback trigger when cross-region error delta > 5% for 2 consecutive min.

jordan: we'll keep the incident open for a 30m stabilization window. Handoff to daytime oncall @sophia in 25m. Sophia, please take over if stable and run postmortem timeline.

sophia: ack handoff. I'll be watching dashboards and will run the postmortem once we confirm 30m of stable metrics. Assigning incident owner role to jordan and postmortem owner to maria-infra. :spiral_calendar_pad: :thumbsup:

jordan: final note before handoff: saving artifacts — bgp_dump.txt, route_table_before.json, route_table_after.json, rollout_history.log. Also creating a customer impact summary for SRE/CS.

ops-bot: Incident P1 mitigated -> monitoring. incident_id=inc_319999. Status: rolling to resolved if no regressions by 3199992100.

sophia: thanks team. We'll run the RCA and follow-up tasks in the postmortem doc. Leaving channel open for final notes.
